sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Library list with versions
sections.what: Names each library the service installs and the version it must match, so the same libraries load on each build.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list keeps builds predictable. Reason for the open versions on the two machine learning libraries is not stated.
sections.watch_out: Upgrading a core library such as FastAPI or Pydantic can break others that depend on it, so test after any change.

summary: Lists the Python libraries the AI service needs and the versions to install.
purpose: Lets someone install the same libraries to run or build the service.
why: Likely reason: fixing versions makes installs repeatable. The reason for open versions on two libraries is not stated.
how: Lists the web framework and server, settings loader, OpenAI client, LangChain packages, Pinecone client, Redis client, HTTP client, structured logging, token counter, the sentence-transformers library, and PyTorch. Most versions are fixed; the last two only set minimum versions.
inputs: Read by pip during the Docker build or a local install.
outputs: Installed libraries available to the service.
risks: The open minimum versions for PyTorch and sentence-transformers can resolve to different versions over time. PyTorch is very large. It is not visible whether LangChain, Pinecone, Redis, or structlog are used by the visible code.
debug: If an install fails, check the Python version against the Dockerfile (3.12) and whether PyTorch can be downloaded. Compare installed versions with this list.
